operatorProperties.code:
def process(worldcities, romanCities) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    wc = worldcities.copy()
    rc = romanCities.copy()

    # Ensure numeric types
    wc['lat'] = pd.to_numeric(wc['lat'], errors='coerce')
    wc['lng'] = pd.to_numeric(wc['lng'], errors='coerce')
    wc['population'] = pd.to_numeric(wc['population'], errors='coerce')

    rc['Latitude (Y)'] = pd.to_numeric(rc['Latitude (Y)'], errors='coerce')
    rc['Longitude (X)'] = pd.to_numeric(rc['Longitude (X)'], errors='coerce')

    # Filter modern cities by population threshold (strictly over 100k)
    wc_f = wc[(wc['population'] > 100_000) & wc['lat'].notna() & wc['lng'].notna()].copy()
    rc_f = rc[rc['Latitude (Y)'].notna() & rc['Longitude (X)'].notna()].copy()

    # Cross join (bounded later by near filter)
    wc_f['_k'] = 1
    rc_f['_k'] = 1
    pairs = wc_f.merge(rc_f, on='_k', how='inner', suffixes=('_wc', '_rc'))

    # Within 0.1 degrees in BOTH latitude and longitude
    near = pairs[(pairs['lat'] - pairs['Latitude (Y)']).abs() <= 0.1]
    near = near[(near['lng'] - near['Longitude (X)']).abs() <= 0.1]

    count = near['id'].nunique(dropna=True)
    return pd.DataFrame({'count': [int(count)]})

operators.customDisplayName: Count distinct modern cities from worldcities with population > 100,000 that lie within 0.1 degrees in BOTH latitude and longitude of at least one Roman-era city from roman_cities: coerce worldcities[lat,lng,population] and romanCities[Latitude (Y),Longitude (X)] to numeric; filter wc population>100k and non-null coords; cross join via constant key; filter |lat-Latitude (Y)|<=0.1 and |lng-Longitude (X)|<=0.1; return single-row DataFrame with integer 'count' = nunique(worldcities.id).
